title: Pedestrians: Children, Older & Disabled People
whatItIs: Pedestrians are the road users most at risk. Children, older people and disabled people need the most care.
keyFacts: Watch for children near schools, parks, ice cream vans and buses: they can run out without looking.
Older people may need more time to cross and may not see or hear you coming.
Someone with a white cane may be blind or partially sighted. A white cane with a red band: they may be deafblind.
Powered wheelchairs and mobility scooters can travel at up to 8 mph on the road: give them room.
Give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you are turning into or out of.

items.title: Children
items.text: Small, quick and hard to see. They can step out from behind parked cars.

items.title: Older people
items.text: May be slower and may misjudge your speed.

items.title: White cane
items.text: The person may be blind or partially sighted.

items.title: White cane with a red band
items.text: The person may be deafblind: they may not see or hear you.

items.title: Assistance dogs
items.text: The person may be blind or have another disability.

items.title: Wheelchairs and scooters
items.text: Slow, low and may use the road where there is no pavement.

b.label: White cane with a red band
points: May not see or hear you

onTheTest.question: You see a pedestrian with a white cane with a red band. What does this mean?
options: They may be deaf and blind
They are training a guide dog
onTheTest.why: A white cane with a red band means the person may be deafblind, so they may not see you or hear your horn.

traps: Don't sound your horn to warn a deafblind person: they may not hear it.
Children can appear from behind parked cars, buses and ice cream vans.
Where there is no pavement, people may walk in the road: give them room.

sources.ref: Rules 204 to 210 (Road users requiring extra care)
